lines.trans: Stay out there with her at least until her van arrives.
About missing the movie tonight… no, I mean I was the one who really regretted missing it.
If what I said to you last time upset you, I truly apologize.
Not at all, that is just who I am—plenty of people curse me out as a super-fake brat anyway.
I once heard that malicious words spoken behind your back are like arrows dipped in poison.
Thankfully, words shot from hiding lack strength, so those arrows cannot pierce your chest.
The most foolish thing of all is picking up that fallen arrow off the ground and plunging it into your own heart.
Taking wounds you never needed to suffer—I truly hope you will not do that to yourself, Ms. Cindy.
Senior Ye-jin booked the tickets, so I do not really know which movie it was either—since we missed it anyway.
So it did not matter at all what movie was playing—you went not to watch a film, but to see Producer Ye-jin.

Goodbye! (go safely)

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

examples.text: 저희 어머님은 가수 전영록 씨 노래를 들으면 아직도 옛날 연애하던 좋았던 시절이 생각나서 가슴이 떨리고 좋으시답니다.
examples.trans: Whenever my mother hears singer Jeon Young-rok's songs, her heart still flutters happily remembering the sweet days when she was young and in love.
This point about her heart is really important.
Goodbye! (go safely)
Let us do that (go (honorific)) right away.

examples.text: 아니에요, 저 원래 그러는데요. 많은 사람들이 나 가식 쩌는 왕싸가지라고 욕하잖아요.
examples.trans: Not at all, that is just who I am—plenty of people curse me out as a super-fake brat anyway.
This point about pretense, fakery is really important.

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'the most' is key.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?
Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.
So let's go.
Therefore it is good.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this someone else's?
I was busy today because of someone else's.

examples.text: 다행히 뒤에 숨어서 하는 말은 힘이 없어서 그 화살이 내 가슴을 뚫지는 못한대요.
examples.trans: Thankfully, words shot from hiding lack strength, so those arrows cannot pierce your chest.
I thought it over again (thankfully).

examples.text: 남들이 뒤에서 나를 헐뜯는 말은 독이 묻은 화살 같은 거랍니다.
examples.trans: I once heard that malicious words spoken behind your back are like arrows dipped in poison.
This point about poison is really important.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

examples.text: 그래서 요 며칠 내 뒤를 졸졸 따라다니면서 선배를 떠봐?
examples.trans: So that is why you trailed behind me like a puppy these past few days sounding out your senior?
Here the word for 'behind me' is key.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 주다, used when giving to elders or superiors.

examples.trans: I gave a present to my grandmother.
May I ask you a question?

examples.text: 땅 짚고 헤엄치기, 누워서 떡 먹기! 혼자 보기 아깝고 말하기는 입 아파요.
examples.trans: Swimming with your hands on the bottom, eating rice cake lying down—too funny to watch alone and exhausting to describe!
This point about the ground is really important.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.
I want to fall off, you know right now.
How about trying to fall off, you know together tomorrow?

examples.text: 다행히 뒤에 숨어서 하는 말은 힘이 없어서 그 화살이 내 가슴을 뚫지는 못한대요.
examples.trans: Thankfully, words shot from hiding lack strength, so those arrows cannot pierce your chest.
Let us do that (pierce through) right away.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.en: words, remarks (humble when referring to one's own speech to a superior)
meanings.note: Used in 말씀을 드리다 ('to tell/inform a superior').

meanings.en: words, speech (honorific when referring to a superior's speech)

examples.trans: I spoke to the teacher.
Thank you for your kind words.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.
Dirt got on the clothes.
Yes, that's right.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

examples.text: 그러니까 어떤 영화인지는 상관이 없었다? 영화를 보러 간 게 아니라 예진 피디님을 보러 간 거네.
examples.trans: So it did not matter at all what movie was playing—you went not to watch a film, but to see Producer Ye-jin.
This point about matter, relevance is really important.

examples.text: 받지 않아도 되는 상처를 받고… 신디 씨는 그러지 않으셨으면 좋겠습니다.
examples.trans: Taking wounds you never needed to suffer—I truly hope you will not do that to yourself, Ms. Cindy.
This point about wounds is really important.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Literally 'one's inside hurts'; describes emotional distress.

examples.trans: I'm upset because I did poorly on the exam.
Don't be too upset.

examples.text: 악플 이런 거 하나도 안 무서워, 모니터 뒤에 숨어서 입만 나불대는 것들!
examples.trans: Malicious comments do not scare me one bit—cowards hiding behind monitors just flapping their mouths!
Let us do that (hiding and) right away.
Did you hear about this Ms.?
I was busy today because of Ms..

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
No, I'm okay.
No, I haven't eaten yet.

examples.text: 1년에 한 번이라는 게 아쉬울 정도고 분기마다 했으면 좋겠습니다, 진짜!
examples.trans: Once a year honestly feels way too rare—I wish we held sports day every single quarter!
It is really regrettable, too rare compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

examples.text: 가장 어리석은 행동은 땅에 떨어진 그 화살을 내가 주워서 내 가슴에 찌르는 거죠.
examples.trans: The most foolish thing of all is picking up that fallen arrow off the ground and plunging it into your own heart.
It is really foolish compared to what I expected.
Stop, that is enough—it was all a lie anyway!
Here the word for 'anyway, in any case' is key.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Let's go watch a movie.
What movie is it?

examples.text: 그건 예진 선배님이 예매를 하신 거라 저도 어떤 영화였는지는 잘… 어차피 못 봐서요.
examples.trans: Senior Ye-jin booked the tickets, so I do not really know which movie it was either—since we missed it anyway.
This point about advance booking is really important.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun + casual copula (왕싸가지야!).

examples.text: 근데 신디 걔는 며칠을 같이 지냈는데 어쩜 잘 들어갔다는 소식이 없냐? 은혜도 모르는 아주 왕싸가지야!
examples.trans: Still, Cindy stayed here for days—how has she sent zero word that she got back safely? What an ungrateful brat!
This point about is a total brat is really important.

examples.text: 너는 남자 아이돌은 욕 안 하잖아, 여자 아이돌만 욕하지.
examples.trans: You never criticize male idols—you only criticize female idols.
This expression comes from 'you badmouth'.

meanings.note: refers to an initial state or plan

examples.trans: Traffic is usually heavy on Mondays.
This place was originally a park.

examples.text: 고맙다, 가랄 때 안 가고 옆에 있어줘서.
examples.trans: Thank you for not leaving when I told you to go and staying beside me.
Let us do that (for staying for me) right away.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

examples.text: 가장 어리석은 행동은 땅에 떨어진 그 화살을 내가 주워서 내 가슴에 찌르는 거죠.
examples.trans: The most foolish thing of all is picking up that fallen arrow off the ground and plunging it into your own heart.
Let us do that (picking up and) right away.
I saw it last time.
We decided at the last meeting.

examples.text: 아니에요, 저 원래 그러는데요. 많은 사람들이 나 가식 쩌는 왕싸가지라고 욕하잖아요.
examples.trans: Not at all, that is just who I am—plenty of people curse me out as a super-fake brat anyway.
Let us do that (dripping with (slang)) right away.

examples.text: 가장 어리석은 행동은 땅에 떨어진 그 화살을 내가 주워서 내 가슴에 찌르는 거죠.
examples.trans: The most foolish thing of all is picking up that fallen arrow off the ground and plunging it into your own heart.
Let us do that (stabbing) right away.
This is my father's car.
I parked the car in the parking lot.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

examples.text: 요즘 불만이 극에 달해 있어요, 우리가 단체 행동을 해서 버릇을 고쳐놔야 돼!
examples.trans: Complaints have reached a boiling point lately—we need collective action to fix that attitude!
Here the word for 'action' is key.

examples.text: 남들이 뒤에서 나를 헐뜯는 말은 독이 묻은 화살 같은 거랍니다.
examples.trans: I once heard that malicious words spoken behind your back are like arrows dipped in poison.
Let us do that (slandering, tearing down) right away.
Editing is an arrow—it has to pierce right through people's hearts.
Here the word for 'it is an arrow' is key.

examples.text: 잊지 않고 꼭 갚아 줄 수 있어야 피디한테 힘이 생겨.
examples.trans: Only when people know you remember and repay every debt does a producer gain power.
The topic of power, leverage came up during this shoot.
